sections.content:
24,955 people

were counted on the census as "health associate professionals (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
People who do this type of work carry out a variety of technical health support functions not elsewhere classified.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "health associate professionals (other)" there were more women than men (84% compared with 16%).

This means "health associate professionals (other)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health and social care associate professionals".

Men made up 16% and women made up 84% of "health associate professionals (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "health associate professionals (other)" included:

  • dancers and choreographers
  • child and early years officers
  • pharmaceutical technicians

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "health associate professionals (other)", 14.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "health associate professionals (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "health associate professionals (other)" included:

  • welfare professionals (other)
  • other vocational and industrial trainers
  • housing officers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "health associate professionals (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "health associate professionals (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "health associate professionals (other)", 13.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (50% compared with 50%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (61.6%) than self-employed (38.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
